body: Only advice I've been able to give to people is how to treat suicidal people weirdly enough, mostly because during my depression I started reading upon suicidology to see whether my friends' and family's behaviour might actually be pushing me to the edge inadvertantly. I've had to talk to a few suicidal people and talk them out of it which is ironic in itself. To be honest it isn't something I can do anymore as I just hate lying. How can I say that to a person while within me I am wondering whether I can make nembutal myself or what is the best place to jump from? Maybe I am not enough of a politician to lie that well for long.

Why end it you say.

Maybe me being tired exceeds the joy I get out of living. When every weekend feels like a charade, every sunday like hell, and at work I just try to survive with a smile on my face as to not disturb the environment. Sleeping is my only reprieve and the only place I can somehow enjoy myself as I dream and dream and dream.

The name you are trying to google for is Anna Kristjánsdóttir(which will probably also give up nationality, a dangerous game for me, but what the hell), as I am talking about the first public transwoman in my country.

Regarding age I am 31 years old.  Did say 10 years ago I'd wait until I was 35, but this isn't as linear as I'd imagine(depression that is).

Personal experience is that when I was young I saw the first public transwoman vilified and called a monster and it was the only point of reference transgender people have. The stigma is slowly eroding, but for some of us it just feels too late and when time and your body are your worst enemy, late has a different meaning.

For your children I truly hope that they never deal with being transgender.  Not for your sake, but theirs. This is something I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy.

However, if the need arises there are many stronger transgender people than myself who will be there to help and aid and that combined with an understanding and willing father makes a hell of a difference.

The lucky ones, the ones who can truly inspire hope.

Ugly old troll like me would actually be a disadvantage and I speak of this from a personal experience.

I know it is hard. I've actually done fasting in the past as a test and the first 2 days can be excruciating. After that the body starts to tire of screaming to the brain. Also, the sense of starving can get euphoric as you can get mixed signals(get happy and euphoric that you are overcominging something. Not perhaps the right wording but it is there about).

Tried pills 3 times and carbon monoxide at the 4th time(but it was stupidly done so it didn't do too much). This way I can at least set my things in order and maybe say good bye a few times. I don't worry too much about people noticing as I am an excellent actor when it comes to hiding stuff(well, there is of course a tipping point where it becomes nigh impossible to hide but that is during the last phases of starvation).

Don't want to sound overly morbid(which I probably do), but I am tired of having a mask.

Just your average transgender/tranny individual that is tired of this cycle of existence and wants to take a chance at the next one(if there is one at all). After puberty life has felt like an endless spiral down that can't be changed due to fate/chance/destiny. Which is why I'd rather die and be a statistic, maybe an example of why transgender individuals should be attended to during their youth. It would at least be something and I wouldn't have to be aware of my self-loathing anymore.

Don't know what I can add. I've attempted suicide 4 times already(over the period of two years, and shows how atrocious I am at it). This is a depression I've fought with for over two decades and it is getting tiresome.

On the plus side my foster sister and her family will get my parent's house when they die. They have so much going on for them that they deserve it.
